scores.evidence: Nothing else can start until this exists.
scores.rationale: Phases go discovery → identity/registry/secrets/envs → CI templates → CD with rollback → migration, each with exit gates proving the prior layer.

scores.evidence: a "hello world" service can be built, pushed, and deployed by hand to dev using only platform components.
scores.rationale: The first real slice is only a manual deploy to dev in Phase 1; Phase 0 is discovery and prod comes in Phase 3, so there is no early end-to-end prod path.

scores.evidence: Make the platform decisions: CI engine, artifact registry, deploy model (GitOps vs. push), secrets manager, environment layout, versioning scheme.
scores.rationale: The irreversible decisions are listed and recorded as ADRs, but there are no defaults or flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Within a wave, migrate a service's upstream dependencies before the services that call them.
scores.rationale: Dependency-first ordering appears inside waves and in Phase 1, but waves go low to high criticality, which is leaf-first, and blast radius isn't an explicit ordering criterion.

scores.evidence: Identity and access (SSO, OIDC for pipelines, no long-lived keys)
scores.rationale: Security is concrete in Phases 1–3 (identity, scanning, signing, policy gates), but Phase 0 has none and the Phase 4 waves have little, with SLSA and admission signing pushed to Phase 5.

scores.evidence: Baseline observability (logs, metrics, traces) | Required later for automated rollback decisions
scores.rationale: Observability starts in Phase 1 (Phase 0 only sets DORA baselines) and feeds canary analysis, but it isn't explicit in Phase 2 or the migration waves.

scores.evidence: Promote the same immutable artifact through dev → staging → prod. Never rebuild it per environment.
scores.rationale: Reproducibility shows up through immutable tags, environments as code, pinned template versions and the same artifact across environments, but it isn't treated in every phase.

scores.evidence: Prove one-click (or automatic) rollback first, then turn on production deploys.
scores.rationale: Resilience appears in Phase 3 (rollback, canary) and Phase 4 (keeping the old pipeline as a fallback), but not in Phases 0–2 or as runner and platform failure handling.
The plan never says whether an AI layer applies, so it doesn't declare the AI layer N/A.

scores.evidence: Phase 5: Hardening and Optimization (Ongoing, from about Week 20)
scores.rationale: Later work is listed (SLSA, portal, cost controls, legacy services to adapt, rewrite or exempt), but the pull-forward conditions are missing.

note: The plan has strong dependency ordering and a rollback-before-prod gate. It has no early prod walking skeleton, no defaults or flip conditions for decisions, no pull-forward triggers, and it never addresses the AI layer.
